title: Spire of Dublin
visualBrief: Tapered 120 m stainless steel monument, separate reflective geological pattern islands, 11,884 actual tip perforations with plate reveals and internal diffuser, concentric base grating, dark stone surround and eight removable bollards. Reusable polished and bead-blasted material graphs supply the metal finishes.

assembly.method: Reusable named mesh parts with glTF node transforms; shared materials, no duplicated bitmap library.

nativeAxes.origin: Native +X east,+Z south,+Y vertical; heading0 preserves cardinal axes around the mapped circular exact-Q1134365 monument. The cone and grating are axial; reconstructed stencil marks and eight regularized bollards have no certified compass phase. No entrance bearing is asserted.

scaleBasis: Dublin City Council and fabricator dimensions fix the 120 m cone, 3 m base and 150 mm tip. IMOA fixes 11,884 holes of 15 mm diameter over the upper 12 m. Surround/grating/bollards are scaled from the inspected architect photograph, not a site survey.

geographicProposal.evidence: Exact-QID mapped spire polygon provides the centre. Published dimensions supersede the smaller mapped footprint and mapped 121.2 m height.
geographicProposal.limitations: Medium-fi static daylight exterior:120m,3m base and0.15m tip follow fabricator/tourism engineering facts. Exact11884physical15mm holes remain in the original instanced master; budgeted close-up substitutes11884opaque daylight diffuser marks, street/district average subpixel perforations. Base artwork is original geological-strata reconstruction with reduced marks at distance, not a traced full architect stencil or a certified azimuth. Surround8.1m and eight regularized bollards follow inspected early architect photograph, not a current street survey; current grating/bollard phase, maintenance hatches, night beacon and wind animation are outside this daylight scope. Map2.2m ring/121.2m height are not sizing controls. Host terrain sets street datum; no footprint replacement or surrounding streets/rails baked in.
